title: Apple Negotiates Nine-Figure Budget to Pay Publishers for Siri AI Content
excerpt: The iPhone maker is proposing pay-as-you-go deals with news organizations to power its revamped AI assistant, breaking from the industry's standard licensing model.
body:
• Apple is negotiating multiyear deals with news publishers to license their content for its revamped AI-powered Siri assistant, according to The Wall Street Journal.
  • The company has proposed a variable, pay-as-you-go compensation model and discussed a possible nine-figure budget for publisher payments.
  • Siri AI, powered by Google's Gemini, is expected to roll out with iOS 27 this fall after years of criticism over the assistant's limited capabilities.
  • The move comes after Apple's 2024 experiment with AI-generated news roundups produced erroneous headlines, forcing the company to disable the feature.

Apple is in talks with news publishers to pay for access to their content to power Siri AI, the company's upcoming artificial intelligence assistant, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.

The iPhone maker has reached out to publishers in recent months, proposing new multiyear licensing deals that would give Apple access to current news and information to improve Siri's ability to answer questions about real-world events. The company has discussed a possible nine-figure budget for the payments, people familiar with the matter told the Journal.

A Different Model From the Industry Standard

Unlike the guaranteed-fee licensing deals that have become standard between AI companies and publishers, Apple has proposed a variable compensation structure. Publishers would be paid when their content is actually used by Siri AI — essentially a pay-as-you-go arrangement rather than an upfront lump sum for broad access.

https://x.com/wallstengine/status/2087683356783988887

The approach marks a departure from the deals that companies like OpenAI and Google have struck with news organizations, which typically involve fixed annual payments in exchange for wide-ranging training rights. Apple's model could mean lower guaranteed revenue for publishers but potentially higher payouts if Siri AI becomes a primary information source for hundreds of millions of iPhone users.

Apple has previously paid publishers for content access. The company's Apple News+ subscription service, launched in 2019, provided meaningful revenue for a handful of news and magazine publishers, though some have since pulled out. Earlier AI-related deals included training rights for Apple's models.

Siri's Long Road to AI

The publisher outreach comes as Apple works to overhaul Siri, which has faced years of criticism for lagging behind competitors like Google Assistant and Amazon's Alexa. At WWDC 2026 in June, Apple announced "Siri AI" — a major upgrade that integrates Google's Gemini AI model into the assistant, enabling more natural conversations, on-screen awareness, and deeper understanding of personal context.

Siri AI is available now in the iOS 27 developer beta, with a public beta expected this month and a full rollout in September. The upgrade is compatible with iPhone 15 Pro and newer devices.

"We'll see what Siri AI does to the company's costs."

— Tim Cook, Apple CEO, to analysts

Apple's AI strategy has been notably capital-light compared to rivals. The company abandoned an earlier partnership with OpenAI in favor of Google's Gemini, avoiding the massive infrastructure spending that companies like Microsoft and Google have absorbed. But as a WSJ analysis noted, success in AI ultimately requires spending — even for Apple.

Learning From Past Mistakes

The push for licensed publisher content likely reflects lessons from Apple's last brush with AI-generated news. In late 2024, the company began offering users AI-generated news roundups. The tool published erroneous headlines — a serious embarrassment that drew criticism from publishers and prompted Apple to quickly disable the feature.

By licensing current, verified content from established publishers, Apple can reduce the risk of Siri AI generating false or misleading information about current events. For publishers, the arrangement offers a potential new revenue stream at a time when the news industry continues to grapple with declining advertising revenue and the existential question of how AI will reshape content distribution.

What's Next

The negotiations are ongoing, and no deals have been finalized. News Corp, the parent company of The Wall Street Journal, already has a commercial agreement with Apple to supply news through its services. The outcome of these talks could set a template for how AI assistants compensate content creators — a question with implications far beyond Apple and the news industry.

Apple declined to comment on the talks.
nri_angle: The deal could reshape how AI assistants source information globally, affecting how hundreds of millions of users — including the tech-savvy Indian diaspora — access news.
